records.subject: Need for a National Social Media Policy for public office holders.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Rajinder Gupta: In recent years, a disturbing trend is being witnessed. Some senior bureaucrats including IAS and IPS officers, and even functionaries connected to the judiciary are increasingly using personal social media platforms to publicize their official duties. Transparency in governance is important, but public office cannot become a platform for personal publicity. Today we see officers posting dramatic videos of raids, inspections, and enforcement drives on their personal handles, often with cinematic music and carefully staged visuals that project them as individual heroes. Even more worrying is that in several instances information about official actions appears first on personal social media accounts, sometimes before formal government communication. The issue becomes even more sensitive when it concerns judicial officers or court-related functionaries. The judiciary derives its authority from restraint, neutrality, and public trust. Any activity that blurs the line between institutional conduct and personal visibility risks eroding that trust. The All India Services (Conduct) Rules, 1968 and the Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964 were framed in a time when social media did not exist. Today the digital landscape has changed, but our regulatory framework has not kept pace. Therefore, I urge the Government to bring a clear National Social Media Policy for public officials that separates official communication from personal publicity, restricts disclosure of sensitive or sub-judice matters, and establishes accountability when public-office is used for personal branding.

(ENDS)

records.subject: PROMOTION OF RURAL TOURISM
records.extent:
The Government has approved the initiative to develop tribal home-stays under Swadesh
Darshan Scheme, as part of ‘Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan’. The said intervention
includes development of 1000 homestays with support of upto Rs.5 Lakh per unit (for new
construction), up to Rs.3 Lakh (renovation) and Rs.5 Lakh for village community requirement.
